questions.q: For a row to survive an AND condition, what must be true?
options: Every condition joined by AND must be true
At least one condition must be true
Exactly one condition must be true
None of the conditions can be true
questions.explain: AND requires all conditions to hold; a single false condition eliminates the row.

questions.q: For a row to survive an OR condition, what must be true?
options: At least one of the conditions must be true
All conditions must be true
Exactly zero conditions can be true
OR only works with numeric columns
questions.explain: OR only requires one side to be true — unlike AND, which requires both.

options: Where color is not red — functionally similar to Color <> 'Red'
Where color is exactly red
It's invalid syntax in T-SQL
It reverses the sort order of the results
questions.explain: NOT inverts the condition that follows it.

questions.q: In 'WHERE Color = 'Red' OR Color = 'Blue' AND ListPrice > 500' (no parentheses), which operator evaluates first?
options: AND — so it's actually (Color = 'Blue' AND ListPrice > 500), OR'd with Color = 'Red'
OR — so it evaluates strictly left to right
They evaluate simultaneously with no defined order
This is a syntax error without parentheses
questions.explain: AND binds tighter than OR in T-SQL, which is why every red product is included regardless of price in this unparenthesized version.

questions.q: What's the rule of thumb for mixing AND and OR in the same WHERE clause?
options: Always use parentheses to make the intended grouping explicit
Never combine AND and OR in the same query
Always put OR conditions first, no parentheses needed
Parentheses are only needed with three or more conditions
questions.explain: Parentheses remove any ambiguity about which conditions are meant to be grouped together, avoiding a very common class of filtering bug.
